name: Owls
label: Jade Tree
lede: Cap'n Jazz minus Davey von Bohlen makes one Steve Albini-recorded album for Jade Tree, tours it and quits, then comes back ten years later for a second one on Polyvinyl.

eras.title: Before Owls, Cap'n Jazz
eras.text: Before Owls came Cap'n Jazz, the Buffalo Grove, Illinois teenagers whose one album had a title longer than most of its songs. When it ended in 1995, the members scattered into The Promise Ring, Joan of Arc, American Football and more.

years.h: Four Buffalo Grove kids start a band called Toe Jam
years.p: Brothers [[Tim Kinsella|0350b5ce-ab77-4cbf-a550-944b851e4454]] and [[Mike Kinsella|2b5e086f-cb7b-4f92-8a85-6a1c38ceb598]], [[Victor Villarreal|2758e65d-226a-4f21-b1e2-1eb72c4300b1]] and Sam Zurick play as Toe Jam before the name becomes [[Cap'n Jazz|04482c2e-88ab-4709-a412-85748b7ac825]]. Mike takes over drums at 12, when the first drummer quits for football.

years.cap: Cap'n Jazz at Wheeling Palooza, from a high school yearbook page: Tim Kinsella on trumpet, Villarreal and Zurick behind, Mike Kinsella on drums
years.h: Cap'n Jazz plays Little Rock and calls it a day
years.p: The band breaks up after the show, the same year as its only album, known to fans as Shmap'n Shmazz. Guitarist Davey von Bohlen goes on to [[The Promise Ring|63a6fae8-d39e-4de6-bfd4-9bcbf489a565]].

years.h: Jade Tree gathers everything Cap'n Jazz recorded
years.p: The two-disc Analphabetapolothology holds the album, early singles, split releases, demos, outtakes and tracks from the band's farewell show in Chicago.

eras.title: Civil War first, then Owls
eras.text: In mid-2000 Tim Kinsella, busy leading Joan of Arc, called his old Cap'n Jazz bandmates back, all but Davey von Bohlen. They cut one tangled, jazz-limbed record with Steve Albini, toured it, and quit.

years.h: Tim Kinsella calls the band back, and the first name is Civil War
years.p: Tim gets Mike Kinsella on drums, Villarreal on guitar and Zurick on bass. Von Bohlen isn't in it, and they rename themselves Owls.

years.big: "If we are gonna do this, record to tape, record all live, it needs to be Albini."
years.h: Owls record with Steve Albini at Electrical Audio
years.p: That was Tim Kinsella's brief for the debut, cut in Chicago in April 2001 with [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]] engineering.
years.xp: The album runs eight songs and 35 minutes 37 seconds. Cam Lindsay of Exclaim! later noted it was made with "no computers, no abstractions, [and] no experimenting."

years.h: Jade Tree, Cap'n Jazz's old label, signs Owls
years.p: The label that put out the Cap'n Jazz retrospective puts four of its members back on the roster. Pre-orders open in mid-May.

yt: Full live set, Sapphire Supper Club, Orlando, 2001
years.h: Jade Tree releases Owls, the only record of the first run
years.p: Pitchfork gave it a 7.0 and found the band "back in strong form"; Stylus gave it 6.5 and called it "nothing special." AllMusic and the Austin Chronicle both liked it.
years.xp:
Reviewers compared it to [[Pavement|36bfa85f-737b-41db-a8fc-b8825850ffc3]], Captain Beefheart and [[American Football|4ebb5ad3-9018-407d-8c24-c03011ab9ac6]]. Germany's Ox-Fanzine hated it, calling the band terrible.

The Japanese edition on Quattro added a bonus track, Later. Rolling Stone put the album on a 2016 emo list, and Vulture put Everyone Is My Friend on its best emo songs list.

years.h: Mike Kinsella starts Owen, mostly alone
years.p: Owen has Mike playing nearly every instrument himself, recorded mostly at his mother's house. It starts the same year as the Owls album.

yt: Everyone Is My Friend, Michigan Fest 2002
years.h: Owls play CMJ in New York and call it quits
years.p: The split comes after one tour and a set at the CMJ Music Marathon in October 2002. A fan clip from Michigan Fest that year has them playing Everyone Is My Friend.

years.h: Tim Kinsella and Zurick start Make Believe
years.p: Villarreal and Zurick's instrumental band [[Ghosts and Vodka|7f7e1171-393c-4c38-b236-8e4440b83b0d]] has already come and gone by then.

eras.title: Back for a second
eras.text: The 2010 Cap'n Jazz reunion opened the door and Owls walked through it. The second album took eighteen months to write and came out on Polyvinyl instead of Jade Tree.

years.h: Cap'n Jazz reunites at the Empty Bottle
years.p: The band, von Bohlen included, plays Joan of Arc's variety show in Chicago on January 22. Its first official reunion show follows at Louisville's Forecastle Festival on July 10.
years.xp: A hometown Chicago show came a week after Forecastle and sold out in about 48 hours, so a second one was added.

years.cap: Owls at Subterranean, Chicago: Sam Zurick and Tim Kinsella
years.h: Ten years after the split, Owls start writing again
years.p: Tim Kinsella, Mike Kinsella, Villarreal and Zurick get back to work in March as Owls.

years.h: Eighteen months of writing, and the record is done
years.p: Owls announce on Facebook on July 22 that the follow-up to their 2001 album is finished.

years.src: Wikipedia: Owls (band) · Consequence: Owls at Chicago's Subterranean
yt: Acoustic session at West Wing studios, UK, Sept 2014
years.h: Two arrives thirteen years after Owls, on Polyvinyl
years.p: Announced in January, out March 25. Mike Kinsella's [[American Football|4ebb5ad3-9018-407d-8c24-c03011ab9ac6]] reunites the same year.
years.xp: Mike wasn't on drums at Owls' December 19 show at Chicago's Subterranean; Consequence says he was away with the reunited American Football. The setlist mixed new songs with Holy Fucking Ghost and What Whorse You Wrote Id On from the 2001 album.

years.h: Rolling Stone lists Owls among the 40 greatest emo albums
years.p: The 2001 Jade Tree album makes the 2016 list.

years.h: Joan of Arc ends after 25 years
years.p: Tim Kinsella's main band, which he led through every lineup since 1995, breaks up.
